headline: Indian Bank Q2 FY27 Advances Reach Rs 7.23 Lakh Crore
hook: Loan growth outpaces deposits by 4.2 points
summary: Indian Bank reported its Q2 FY27 financial performance with total advances reaching Rs 7.23 lakh crore. During the quarter, the bank's loan growth outpaced deposit growth by 4.2 percentage points. This indicates robust credit demand outpacing deposit mobilization for the lender. For retail investors, widening credit-deposit gaps highlight liquidity management trends in public sector banks.
why_it_matters: Credit growth outstrips deposits at Indian Bank
winners_losers: Indian Bank gains / deposit mobilization constrained

headline: Indian Bank CEO signals possible waiver of 0.28% UPI MDR
hook: Potential shift in UPI transaction fee policy
summary: Indian Bank MD and CEO Shanti Lal Jain stated the bank may consider waiving the 0.28% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions. The executive noted that while MDR implementation would be incrementally positive for bank revenues, the impact on overall income remains minimal. This potential policy shift comes as banks balance UPI adoption growth with fee structures.
why_it_matters: UPI transaction costs may remain zero for merchants
winners_losers: Merchants gain / Banks lose minor fee income

headline: Indian Bank reports 17 percent growth in advances for Q2
summary: Indian Bank recorded a 16.6% year-on-year increase in advances and a 12.4% rise in deposits for the second quarter. Total business for the lender has now reached nearly ₹16 lakh crore. The bank's performance remains consistent with its long-term FY27 guidance. This growth reflects steady credit demand despite current macroeconomic conditions.
why_it_matters: Strong credit growth signals healthy earnings potential for the bank.
winners_losers: Indian Bank gains / No clear losers

headline: Indian Bank updates its Treasury Bills Linked Lending Rates
hook: New borrowing costs kick in October 2026
summary: Indian Bank has announced a revision to its Treasury Bills Linked Lending Rates, taking effect from October 3, 2026. This change alters the benchmark interest rates used for pricing certain loan products offered by the bank. Borrowers tied to this external benchmark will see corresponding adjustments in their loan EMIs. Indian retail investors holding the bank's stock or loans should monitor how loan book yields respond.
whats_next: Rate revision takes effect on 3rd October 2026
why_it_matters: Loan EMIs tied to T-Bills will adjust for borrowers

headline: Indian banks report credit growth outpacing deposits in the second quarter
hook: Loan demand races ahead of deposit growth
summary: In the second quarter, Indian banks saw credit growth significantly outpace deposit growth. Canara Bank reported credit growth of 19.4% against a deposit increase of 13.1%. Indian Bank recorded 16.6% credit growth with deposits rising by 12.4%. South Indian Bank was a notable exception to this nationwide trend.
whats_next: Q3 deposit and credit growth data releases
why_it_matters: Banks may hike deposit rates to chase scarce funds
winners_losers: Savers gain higher rates / Banks face margin pressure
